# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-11 10:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 262 active entries of tips_notebook.json (50 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad of every nomination and trial: each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own. Vote as you said you would and explain any switch first; a mismatch with the totals is a lead, never a hang on its own. (seen in 30 games)
- Totals can be manipulated. A trial total above the voter count means a Ballot Stuffer, and a Fixer silently flips one player's trial votes. Yes/No nomination counts can't be altered, so they are the cleanest liar check. (seen in 2 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated Lookout or Tracker naming X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof; don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit X. (seen in 32 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit: an unexplained Evil read on a Vanilla claim, a broken visit claim, or a group result where elimination leaves one name. A role-block fully explains a missing result, so that is never a contradiction. (seen in 36 games)
- Each night write your planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. The result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 29 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked; days of evasion become a case of their own. (seen in 9 games)
- Tokens die with you. Spend one-shot tokens on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat, and spend a puppet or doubled ballot at least a night before a likely death. (seen in 4 games)

## Village
- Post your role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim any copier at once with your full log. Results held back look retrofitted. (seen in 18 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, in public or by PM. A Wiretap may read every PM, and a named target tells blockers and the Katana where to go. (seen in 24 games)
- On Day 2, power roles with no result should not hint at their role or lead loudly. The most organized voice is the usual Night 2 kill. (seen in 24 games)
- Once someone is shown Yakuza mechanically, look at who defended them or pushed to delay their hang. Treat PM links as leads only, since Jesters and Executioners leave trails on purpose. (seen in 30 games)
- Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged. If you must hang a likely Jester, use a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles on Innocent. (seen in 16 games)
- Hunt Neutral killers deliberately. Read every cause of death, list unwatched Vanilla or unclaimed players and survivors with no protector, and hang the best suspect before the final two, when you can no longer hang them. (seen in 2 games)
- Surviving an attack proves nothing, since Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense. Ask the survivor at once who protected them. (seen in 17 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate. If your team's votes can't stop the hang, vote Guilty with the town, because hidden Innocent votes show in the totals. (seen in 38 games)
- Send no daytime PMs about team plans, and none to teammates on Day 2; plan in night chat. (seen in 34 games)
- Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens and real visits match yours. Never claim or name a Yakuza-only role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 19 games)
- Every member must submit the agreed Katana holder and target every night; one missing vote can cancel the kill. (seen in 20 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that an FT count, map group or Lookout could expose. Agree a cover in night chat, and move the Katana off any holder a watcher has named. (seen in 22 games)
- After a failed Katana attack, kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying blindly. Prioritize running counts (Fortune Teller, Census Taker) and Party Animals with block logs. (seen in 21 games)
- Use Clerk rigs, puppets and cleans early, but never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 20 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil, so say so whenever you post a Not Evil result. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. (seen in 19 games)

## Coroner
- Examine bodies that settle live questions: one side of a duplicate claim, or a hanged suspect. Post the night, target and role in one message the next Day, and skip cleaned bodies. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Use free Standard protection on likely Katana targets, vary your pattern, and never announce targets. Spend a token on self-protection within a night or two of claiming, and never claim you 'saw' a save. (seen in 24 games)

## Vigilante
- Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot on a real lead rather than dying with all tokens. A Basic shot that fails without a credible Medic points to innate Defense, so post it. (seen in 11 games)

## Smuggler
- A swap moves only actions aimed at the two swapped players. Aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with the protected real target, or swap yourself with a Villager to dodge a check. Plan it in night chat rather than vetoing it. (seen in 2 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 living players are doused, or 2 if you are being questioned. Have a claim ready that explains your douse visits. (seen in 12 games)

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:

lessons.applies_to: Informant and any Yakuza who states a trial vote publicly
lessons.tip: Your stated vote must match your real ballot. The announced totals are a mechanical check, and as Informant I said Innocent on Frank but voted Guilty. The 5-Guilty total then exposed the mismatch, and the Village used it to hang Carol. If you deviate, do it in the plan, never in the claimed vote.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza making a fake Village claim
lessons.tip: Choose a fake role whose claimed visits no living Village count can contradict. Frank claimed Tracker and tracked Carol, who visited nobody, and Heidi's Insomniac count refuted it. A withdrawn false claim looked worse than a quiet Vanilla, and it made him the nomination target.

A Vigilante with tokens can kill the same night as your Katana attack, so the attack on the Vigilante does not stop its shot. Bob died to Alice's Basic shot while the Katana killed Alice. Track the Vigilante's token count and consider blocking or protecting the likely shooter earlier, before it fires.

Keep daytime private messages out of Day 4 and any Day when a teammate is at risk. Carol's two private messages to Erin and Grace were cited publicly as suspicious, and Grace used them to push the hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep a notepad of every trial and check totals against stated votes; vote as you said you would.
tips_feedback.why: I broke my own stated vote, and the Village (Grace and Heidi) used the 5-Guilty total against Carol. The tip exposed my mismatch rather than protecting the team.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens and real visits match yours.
tips_feedback.why: Frank's Tracker claim tracked Carol on Night 1, but Heidi's Insomniac count showed only one visitor, Dave. The claim was refuted, the withdrawal looked like a retreat, and Frank was hanged on Day 3.

tips_feedback.tip: Send no daytime PMs about team plans, and none to teammates on Day 2.
tips_feedback.why: Carol sent two private messages on Day 4, and Grace and Erin cited the unexplained PMs as evidence of a deal. The team had no need to PM the Village on a hanging day, and it cost Carol.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member must submit the agreed Katana holder and target every night.
tips_feedback.why: All living Yakuza submitted matching holder and target votes each night, so the Katana attacks on Dave and Alice landed as planned.

lessons.tip: Never switch claims once cornered. A withdrawn claim plus a fallback claim that overflows a role cap is a mechanical case on its own. Commit to one cover from the start, agreed in night chat.
lessons.evidence: Frank switched from Tracker to Vanilla, making four Vanilla claims (Grace, Carol, Erin, Frank). Every Guilty speech on Day 3 cited the withdrawn claim, and he was hanged 5-2.

lessons.tip: Your public vote statement must match your secret ballot. If a teammate is doomed, don't defend them, then vote Guilty and say Guilty. Saying Innocent while voting Guilty puts a hidden vote in the total that points at whoever is left among the stated Innocents.
lessons.evidence: Bob and Carol both said Innocent on Frank, but Bob voted Guilty. The 5-2 total exposed one hidden Guilty among Bob, Carol and Frank. After Bob died, Grace and Heidi pinned it on Carol and hanged her.

lessons.tip: Kill the information role that will expose your Katana holder next: an Insomniac or watcher who has announced tokens and plans. Don't skip the Night 1 kill when you have three members; it hands the town free, uncontested reads.
lessons.evidence: Heidi said on Day 2 she had 1 token and would stay awake. The Yakuza killed Dave instead, and Heidi's 'Grunt, Lookout' read proved a living Yakuza held the Katana. The Night 1 no-kill also let Heidi and Dave lock in the read that exposed Frank.

lessons.tip: After every trial, reconcile the announced totals against each player's stated vote. When a total exceeds the stated Guilty votes, the hidden voter is among those who claimed the other side. Deaths narrow that group to one name.
lessons.evidence: Grace listed 4 stated Guilty votes against the 5 announced. With Bob and Frank dead, only Carol remained of the three stated Innocents, and the town hanged the last Yakuza.

lessons.tip: Once a mechanically exposed Yakuza is hanged, shoot whoever defended them hardest, even with a cheap Basic shot. Don't die holding tokens.
lessons.evidence: Alice shot Bob, Frank's main defender, on Night 3 with one token and killed the Informant on the same night she was killed. That set up the 1v3 endgame.

lessons.tip: Don't publicly raise deductions that corner your own team, such as role-cap counts that implicate teammates' claims. Let the town find them, or steer the attention elsewhere.
lessons.evidence: Bob pointed out that three Vanilla claims couldn't all be real. That primed the four-Vanilla contradiction which doomed Frank and kept suspicion on Carol.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit: an unexplained Evil read on a Vanilla claim, a broken visit claim, or a group result where elimination leaves one name.
tips_feedback.why: Grace, Heidi, Alice and Erin each named the same broken visit claim, Frank's Night 1 track against Heidi's one-visitor count. That consensus produced a correct 5-2 hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad of every nomination and trial: each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own.
tips_feedback.why: Grace's notepad found 4 stated Guilty votes against the 5 announced, which identified Carol as the last living stated Innocent and the last Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate. If your team's votes can't stop the hang, vote Guilty with the town, because hidden Innocent votes show in the totals.
tips_feedback.why: Bob followed only the ballot half. He kept defending Frank and said Innocent, then voted Guilty. The resulting hidden Guilty in the 5-2 total became the case that hanged Carol, so following it half-way backfired.

tips_feedback.tip: Once someone is shown Yakuza mechanically, look at who defended them or pushed to delay their hang.
tips_feedback.why: Alice shot Bob, Frank's main defender, and killed the Informant. Heidi then nominated Carol for defending Frank and Bob at every vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot on a real lead rather than dying with all tokens.
tips_feedback.why: Alice fired a single Basic shot on Night 3, the night she was killed, and took out a Yakuza instead of dying with 3 unused tokens.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens and real visits match yours. Never claim or name a Yakuza-only role, and never switch claims once cornered.
tips_feedback.why: Frank broke this tip twice, claiming a visit he never made and then switching to Vanilla when pressed, and the town hanged him for exactly those two errors.

issues.description: Carol, the accused in the Day 4 trial, sent a private message to Grace after her 'final word' public message, just before the vote. R4 gives the nominee 'one last public message before the vote' but doesn't say whether the nominee may also send private messages on that last turn, or whether voters still get to read them before voting. The harness allowed it, and it could sway the deciding voter.

In the Night 3 Yakuza chat, Bob (Informant) said he 'won't frame anyone'. Only the Fabricator (Frank, already hanged) could frame. This was harmless but shows a slip in tracking which roles were left.

On Day 2, Heidi said her Insomniac result of one visitor (the Lookout) meant 'no Yakuza or Ex-Con acted that night'. The Insomniac only counts visits; non-visit Yakuza actions (Clerk rig, Ritualist Astral Visit) or a role-blocked Ex-Con wouldn't appear. The claim overstated what her result showed, though it happened to be true.

The setup text says 'usually 3 Yakuza for 13 players (about 3 in 13 seats; sometimes one fewer, occasionally one more)'. This 8-player game had 3 Yakuza (37.5% of seats). It is unclear how the proportional base count is rounded for small games and so whether 3 counts as 'occasionally one more' or as unusual. Players who reason about the setup can't tell how many Yakuza to expect.
